To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ANG II activates c-Src in rat PVSMCs, which contributes to the contractile response to the peptide.
Src family kinases play a role in the rat preglomerular contractile response to angiotensin II.
Src family kinase(s), particularly c-Src, are activated by ANG II, and Src family kinase(s)-mediated effects contribute to ANG II-induced preglomerular vasmotor tone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the nonreceptor tyrosine kinase Src family in the regulation of preglomerular microvessel function.
the regulation of renal vascular tone by ANG II and its role in the development and maintenance of hypertension.
the role of the Src family kinase c-Src and its involvement in ANG II-mediated vasoconstriction of the preglomerular microvasculature of the rat kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Src family kinase activation contributes to the afferent arteriole contractile response to angiotensin II.
Src kinase activity is required for full activation of the afferent arteriole by ANG II.
Src family kinases are activated by ANG II in preglomerular microvasculature and that this is associated with an increase in [Ca2+]I and a contractile response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Src family kinase activation is an important component of ANG II-induced preglomerular vasaconstriction and that this activation contributes to ANG II-induced [Ca2+](i) increases in preglomerular smooth muscle cells.
Src kinases play an important role in the preglomerular microvasculature in mediating the contractile responses to ANGII.
ANG II evokes preglomerular vasa constriction via a mechanism that involves Src family kinase activation, which contributes to the [Ca2+](i) response to ANGII.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the preglomerulus has a unique response to ANGII, and this is mediated by the activation of Src kinase.

Src kinase inhibition reduces ANG II-induced vasoconstriction and [Ca2+](i) responses in rat preglomerulus microvessels and that these effects are likely due to Src kinase inhibition of c-Src phosphorylation.
c-Src is a key component of the signaling pathway that couples the ANG II type 1 receptor to the [Ca2+] i response and contractile response of the afferent arteriole.
